articles.content: A judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from seeking early license renewals from ABC stations, finding that the network has faced a “campaign of retaliation” for its protected speech. The FCC ordered Disney-owned ABC in April to file renewal applications for its eight owned stations, including WABC-TV New York, KABC-TV Los Angeles and WLS-TV Chicago. The FCC’s action came a few days after Jimmy Kimmel, the network’s late night host, joked that the First Lady had “a glow like an expectant widow,” which prompted President Trump to call for Kimmel’s firing. Under Brendan Carr, Trump’s appointee to chair the FCC, the agency has opened an investigation of ABC’s daytime talk show “The View” and its interviews of political candidates. articles.content: Brad Pitt has settled his legal battle with ex-wife Angelina Jolie over the sale of her stake in the couple’s winery in France. Pitt sued Jolie in 2022, accusing her of selling her 50% share in Château Miraval to a subsidiary of Stoli, the Russian spirits company, without Pitt’s approval. articles.content: “ Grand Theft Auto VI ” took less than 24 hours to generate $3.79 billion in global sales . That’s roughly 15 percent of the year’s worldwide box office — in under a day. But Hollywood’s biggest concern about games might not be what else consumers are spending their money on. It could be just how many days, weeks, or even months people end up playing “GTA VI” instead of streaming movies or TV on other platforms. Even before Rockstar’s record-breaking launch on November 19, entertainment news outlets like TheWrap were asking whether the game studio’s historic release would seriously disrupt the attention economy . Several analysts echoed that concern in their own industry assessments, warning investors that the sprawling open-world adventure could monopolize living-room airspace until well after the holidays . Personally speaking, as a former video game critic who now mostly covers film and television, I’m fascinated by the competition for both audience engagement and consumer interest. Still, that particular side of “GTA VI” discourse drives me up the wall. Games, movies, TV shows, and social media feeds do indeed battle for our attention, and the business of entertainment is ultimately all about influencing how strangers use their free time. articles.title: Veruschka Dies: German Supermodel Of The 1960s & ’70s Who Appeared In ‘Blow-Up’ Was 87
articles.content: Veruschka , the German supermodel of the 1960s and ’70s who appeared in Michelangelo Antonioni’s iconic Swinging London film Blow-Up and was christened by photographer Richard Avedon as “the most beautiful woman in the world,” has died. She was 87. Her death was announced by Germany newspaper Bild . A cause of death has not been disclosed, but Bild reports that she died surrounded by friends and family at her home in Berlin. Various media reports indicate November 24 as the date of her death. Born Vera Gottliebe Anna Gräfin von Lehndorff-Steinort into German aristocracy on May 14, 1939, in Königsberg, East Prussia, Germany, Veruschka was only 5 when, according to Vogue magazine, her father, Count Heinrich von Lehndorff-Steinort, was executed following a failed 1944 plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler. By age 20, Veruschka had moved to Florence, where she began modeling after meeting photographer Ugo Mulas. Within a couple years she had adopted the Russian-sounding name Veruschka, a moniker befitting her statuesque frame and stark, even severe beauty. By the mid-1960s she had moved to New York, was modeling for the Ford Modeling Agency and on her way to becoming what was considered Germany’s first supermodel. articles.title: Doc Talk Podcast: ‘The Eyes Of Ghana’s Ben Proudfoot & Nana Frimpong On Their Oscar Contender Backed By The Obamas & IShowSpeed
articles.content: Director Ben Proudfoot ’s Oscar-contending documentary The Eyes of Ghana has attracted some impressive supporters, including former occupants of the White House. Former President Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama are among the executive producers of the nonfiction feature through their Higher Ground production company. How could you possibly top that? Well, in addition to the Obamas, The Eyes of Ghana has gained the backing of Darren Watkins Jr, better known to his fans as IShowSpeed , who, according to some measures, is the most popular livestreamer on the planet. In fact, Speed is about to release the film for free on his YouTube channel . Two-time Oscar winner Proudfoot and producer Nana Frimpong join the latest edition of Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast to discuss their film, which is vying to make the Motion Picture Academy’s nonfiction feature shortlist (voting for that begins December 7). The documentary tells the story of a remarkable man named Chris Hesse, now in his 90s, who served as the personal cinematographer to Ghana’s first president, Kwame Nkrumah. In that role, Hesse captured extraordinary footage of the pan-Africanist leader who showed the way for many other countries on the continent to shed their colonial rulers and emerge into independence. Hesse’s invaluable archive was thought to have been lost forever, but Proudfoot and team discovered otherwise. The director and his producer explain the unlikely course of events that revealed the existence of the precious materials in a London hideaway. They also tell us how Barack and Michelle Obama came on board, and how they connected with YouTuber Speed. Proudfoot also shares how he enlisted his friend Kris Bowers, his co-director on the Oscar-winning The Last Repair Shop , to compose the score for The Eyes of Ghana and where they recorded the music — at a place closely associated with The Beatles. articles.content: The holidays have arrived early, as HBO Max has revealed that its critically acclaimed medical drama, The Pitt , will premiere its third season on January 7, 2027. Offering a real-time format, the series traces, hour by hour, the medical cases and personal crises physicians and nurses must navigate as they reckon with an overabundance of patients and a lack of resources. articles.title: ‘South Park’ Celebrates ‘GTA VI’ But Outages, AI Data Centers & Zombie Kenny Stand In The Way In Season 29 Finale
articles.content: As the long wait for Grand Theft Auto VI finally ends, South Park ‘s celebration was cut short on this week’s episode. In the finale “City Endings,” outages hit the town (currently rebranded as South America for Season 29) thanks to the AI data centers of Billionaire Weenietown that moved into Butters’ backyard after Mayor McDaniels cut a deal to bring them to town. A mob visits the mayor, who instead of taking responsibility, leads them to believe the outages are “definitely cyber attacks by the Chinese.” That prompts the mob to stake out Mr. Kim’s City Parlor, where they each end up getting a massage with a “city ending.” Watch on Deadline Meanwhile, Kyle, Stan and Cartman are visited by the ghost of Kenny, who previously died when a bomb strapped to his e-bike exploded. The trio gives Butters a visit after remembering his connectivity issues while trying to watch Dr. Pimple Popper videos. It turns out, Butters is no longer affected by the outages as he’s since been getting some kickbacks from Billionaire Weenietown, including a massive GTA VI setup. In the middle of Butters’ gameplay, zombie Kenny appears on the screen, breaking out like Samara in The Ring to deliver a message to his friends. The episode culminates with the kids confronting the cops and the mayor, only to find out they were all complicit in Kenny’s death when they allowed the billionaires to come to South Park. Ultimately, Mayor McDaniels takes responsibility for the billionaires ruining the town but sends Mr. Kim to space on WeenieX in order to appease the town. The show ends with “America” falling off the South Park sign after they rolled over to change the town’s name for Trump. South Park ‘s finale wrapped up its Billionaire Weenietown storyline with some more topical jabs, following the massively unprecedented release of GTA VI , as well as the ongoing nationwide outages , which the government has chalked up to many networks changing over to AI systems .

articles.content: Hisham Fqih's blend of Saudi mythology and classic Hollywood horror screens at the Doha Film Festival as director notes the 'privilege' of having to learn filmmaking in a digital world before cinemas reopened in the Kingdom in 2016 Over the last six months, a conversation has taken over Hollywood: can the unimaginable success of films like “Backrooms” and “Obsession” usher in the YouTube Age? For Saudi filmmakers, this is a decade-long conversation, driven by a wave of filmmakers raised in a country with no cinemas, who relied on online platforms for production and distribution. When cinemas reopened in Saudi Arabia in 2016, there was no filmmaking tradition in place, but there was already a significant generation of YouTube makers, spearheaded by entertainment company Telfaz11. articles.title: Veruschka, Supermodel Who Appeared in ‘Blow-Up,’ ‘Casino Royale,’ Dies at 87
articles.content: Veruschka, the striking 1960s and ’70s supermodel who inspired some of Richard Avedon ‘s most iconic images and appeared in films including Michelangelo Antonioni’s “Blow-Up,” has died. She was 87. Standing over six feet tall, “Veruschka, with her high forehead, sculptural cheekbones, and elongated limbs, was one of the decade’s most arresting presences, whatever aesthetic she took on,” wrote Vogue in its obituary. She appeared on 13 American Vogue covers. Related Stories Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony Gets Fired Up With Live-Wire Numbers From U2, the Chili Peppers, Usher, Cynthia Erivo, Sienna Spiro, Aerosmith and More Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Designates the Troubadour as a Landmark Venue; Going Forward, L.A. Will Host Hall's Induction Ceremony 'At Least Every Other Year' (EXCLUSIVE) Born Vera Gottliebe Anna Gräfin von Lehndorff-Steinort in East Prussia, she came from a family of aristocrats. Her father joined the German resistance and was executed when she was 5 years old for being involved in the plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler. She was discovered in Italy when she was an art student and became a model, and after meeting Eileen Ford in Paris, she moved to New York. In addition to her brief appearance as herself in the iconic 1966 film “Blow-Up,” she appeared in several other films including the 2006 version of “Casino Royale,” in Franc Roddam’s 1985 “The Bride” and in the 1970 “Salome.” In “Casino Royale,” Veruschka appears as one of only two female poker players at a table with Daniel Craig’s James Bond, Le Chiffre and Felix Leiter. She worked with top photographers including David Bailey, Irving Penn, Steven Meisel, Francesco Scavullo and Peter Beard, and worked for fashion houses including YSL, Helmut Lang and Paco Rabanne. Italian photographer Franco Rubartelli, who created many of the most arresting images of her, was her romantic partner for nine years. She returned to modeling several times in more recent years, including for Acne Studios in 2018.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65
articles.content: Guitarist Andy Taylor , whose tenure in England’s glammy, pop-savvy rock band Duran Duran coincided with the group’s commercial pinnacle of the early ‘80s, died of prostate cancer at his home on Monday while surrounded by family. He was 65. In a statement shared with Variety , Taylor’s wife Tracey said on behalf of their family, “To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather. He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home.” Related Stories 'Murder of JonBenet Ramsey' Trailer Puts Child's Parents Under the Microscope 'Dune: Prophecy' Star Tabu Joins YRF Entertainment's Netflix Rescue Drama 'Tunnel Men' (EXCLUSIVE) Duran Duran added, “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.” Taylor, who was diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, had opted out on appearing at the group’s November 2022 induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, citing a decline in his health in a statement. He said, “Although my current condition is not immediately life-threatening there is no cure…. Recently I was doing OK after some very sophisticated life-extending treatment, that was until a week or so ago when I suffered a setback, and despite the exceptional efforts of my team, I had to be honest in that both physically and mentally, I would be pushing my boundaries.

articles.title: U2 Salutes Dolly Parton With Recreation of Their ‘Torn’ Duet in NFL Thanksgiving Eve Halftime Show
articles.content: U2 paid tribute to Dolly Parton as part of its halftime performance Wednesday night at the NFL ‘s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. The “duet” between a live Bono and a recording of Parton from last summer was the centerpiece of a highly promoted 10-minute set between halves of the contest between the Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers, streamed exclusively on Netflix . U2 did not attempt to cram as many songs into their brief performance as other superstars have during halftime performances, getting in four. The band opened with an abridged “Sunday Bloody Sunday” and ended with “”Pride (in the Name of Love)” and Where the Streets Have No Name” — only squeezing in one song from their new album, the Parton duet, “Torn,” with images of Dolly projected onto three huge curtains that dropped around their stage at the 50-yard line. U2 was also joined by the Womack Sisters , a vocal trio that has just been nominated for best new artist at the Grammys. The dancers first appeared as part of “Sunday Bloody Sunday,” which included an interpolation of the Supremes’ “Stop in the Name of Love,” rendered as something more somber, as performed by the Womack Sisters, to better fit in with U2’s theme of civil war. Bono repeated the “torn” part of that early ’80s anthem as a segue into the song “Torn,” as he and the spectral Parton harmonized on the recent song about a family at war. articles.title: Amanda Seyfried Reveals Secret Elizabeth Holmes Role in ‘You Can See Everything’ Required a “Five-Factor Authentication App” to Read Script
articles.summary: "How the hell did I manage to keep it under wraps?,” the actress joked.
articles.content: Amanda Seyfried is revealing more about the secrecy surrounding her involvement in A24’s You Can See Everything and how she’s surprised she managed to keep her role in the film under wraps. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim , the documentary follows the 34 days the filmmakers spent with disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans , leading up to Holmes’ imprisonment. While Fielder and Oppenheim have worked on the doc for the past three years, Seyfried joined a year ago, appearing as herself and playing Holmes in the film’s third act, after she leaves for prison. Until the film’s October release, Seyfried’s role was kept secret. Related Stories Movies Watch Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's Full In-Depth Breakdown of 'You Can See Everything' Movies 'You Can See Everything' Now Streaming: Where to Watch Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes Doc Online During a new appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , Seyfried opened up about just how secret her participation was. “I didn’t know what the script would be until I got to set, or it would be, like, a five-factor authentication app where I could maybe read it the night before,” she said. You Can See Everything marked Seyfried’s second time playing Holmes , following her portrayal in the 2022 limited series The Dropout . Holmes herself watched clips of Seyfried’s performance in the documentary. Seyfried won an Emmy for her portrayal, and now her latest turn as Holmes is generating Oscar buzz . If she wins the Academy Award, she would make history as the first person to win both an Oscar and an Emmy for playing the same person. Although Seyfried kept her participation in the film private for the better part of a year, she did tell some of those closest to her. “I’m the most indiscreet person I’ve ever met in my life. articles.summary: Dunesday is living up to the expectation as the high-profile features hit tracking.
articles.content: Dunesday excitement is prepared to reach a fever pitch as Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three hit tracking services ahead of their shared release date. Marvel Studios ‘ Avengers: Doomsday is tracking for a massive box office opening of $270 million, marking NRG’s highest starting point ever. Disney releases directors Anthony Russo and Joe Russo’s film on Dec. 18, which is the same day that Warner Bros.’ similarly anticipated Dune: Part Three will hit theaters. As it stands, this launch would mark the strongest domestic opening for December, surpassing 2021’s $260 million start for fellow MCU title Spider-Man: No Way Home . Only this year’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day ($360 million) and 2019’s Avengers: Endgame ($357 million) had higher-grossing openings than No Way Home. Due to the strength of the holiday corridor, when every weekday is known to play like a weekend day, the studio feels confident in the movie’s legs as the excitement surrounding the high-profile frame is likely to benefit all participants. Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Florence Pugh, Anya Taylor-Joy, Jason Momoa and Robert Pattinson round out the cast. Avengers: Doomsday includes an extensive list of Marvel superheroes facing off against Doctor Doom, played by Robert Downey Jr., who is known for his previous Marvel Cinematic Universe role as Tony Stark, aka Iron Man. The Russos helm Avengers: Doomsday from a script by Michael Waldron and Stephen McFeely. The directing duo return to lead an MCU feature for the first time since Avengers: Endgame .

articles.summary: The directors behind A24's unlikely powerhouse Oscar contender joined THR at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival last month, for a live Q&A about the making of the movie. You can now watch it here.
articles.content: When Lance Oppenheim first told his buddy Nathan Fielder that he heard about the potential to make a new documentary about Elizabeth Holmes’ last days before going to prison, Fielder wasn’t sure what tale there was left to tell. There were other docs, books and an Emmy-winning Hulu series out there about her. “I was interested in her, but I didn’t really think there was a story there to do, especially for a doc,” Fielder said last month from the SCAD Savannah Film Festival , where he and Oppenheim joined The Hollywood Reporter for a special post-screening live Q&A (watch it in full below). Moving in with Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans , in her final weeks of freedom — then continuing to make their movie in increasingly daring and surprising directions — Oppenheim and Fielder teamed up for You Can See Everything , one of the most successful theatrical documentaries of all time and a bona fide cultural phenomenon. The movie offers compellingly slippery portraits of both Holmes and Evans, plays off Fielder’s noted screen persona to fascinating effect and features a plum secret role for Amanda Seyfried, who won awards for her portrayal of Holmes in The Dropout (and is now a wildcard Oscar contender). articles.title: How ‘The Other Bennet Sister’ Defied the Odds as a Smash Hit
articles.summary: Stars Ella Bruccoleri and Dónal Finn, as well as executive producer Jane Tranter, joined THR for a special post-screening conversation of the romantic BritBox series, which has been a major success with both audiences and critics.
articles.content: In one of the most sweeping, romantic moments of The Other Bennet Sister , Tom Hayward (Dónal Finn) recites the poem “Composed Upon Westminster Bridge” for Mary Bennet (Ella Bruccoleri), Pride & Prejudice ‘s misfit sibling turned unlikely romantic heroine. The delivery of the poem is wrenching; the scene, in a small rainy garden, idyllic. And yet the scene, adapted by screenwriter Sarah Quintrell from Janice Hadlow’s novel of the same name, was scaled back dramatically from how it reads in the book — taking place against the splendor of the actual Westminster Bridge. Related Stories Lifestyle "Sometimes You Just Have to Think: 'What Will Make People Laugh?'": Lolly Adefope on Gags, 'Ghosts' and Her West End Debut TV NBC to Air Princess of Wales Cancer Charity Documentary “Our budget is a Mary-Bennet-[level], appropriate, ordinary, like-all-of-us sized budget — it’s not a kind of massive franchise genre-tastic kind of thing. It’s humble. We couldn’t film on Westminster Bridge — we just couldn’t afford it,” according to Emmy-winning executive producer Jane Tranter ( Succession ). “We were cramped into this tiny little garden full of rain…to create a scene that just feels so big and so moving and so emotional on very, very little. It’s all about text and performance and intent. That is what The Other Bennet Sister is all about. It’s not flashy or fancy, with loads of money spent on it. It’s about the truth and the emotion.” Audiences have taken note. It’s not just the full-house crowd that packed the San Vicente Bungalows on Friday evening to watch select clips from the series — and catch Tranter alongside Bruccoleri and Finn in conversation — as part of The Hollywood Reporter ’s exclusive THR Frontrunner screening series. articles.title: ‘Hunger Games’ Producer Admits ‘Mockingjay’ Should Have Been One Movie
articles.summary: Franchise producer Nina Jacobson says adapting one book into two movies rubs fans the wrong way: "I think audiences find it cynical."
articles.content: Author Suzanne Collins’ climactic Katniss novel Mockingjay was infamously split into two films, Part 1 and Part 2 . Both are considered a step down from the previous two Hunger Games blockbusters, with lower Rotten Tomatoes critic and audience scores. The uneven Part 1 , in particular, felt like a franchise spinning its wheels. To fans, it all looked like a studio trying to wring more ticket sales from the story. Related Stories Movies Jennifer Lawrence Thinks Her 'Hunger Games' Bow and Arrow Prop Was Stolen Movies 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Review: A Worthier Prequel to the Dystopian Battle Royale, Powered by Joseph Zada's Star-Making Turn In a new interview with Empire , franchise producer Nina Jacobson says that if she and director Francis Lawrence had a second chance, they’d adapt Mockingjay into a single movie. “Even though I love the Mockingjay films, if I had it to do over again, I think both Francis and I might try to do it all in one,” Jacobson said. “ Mockingjay was such a big book, and it takes you to so many different places. But in the end, I think that Francis and I both felt that splitting them up… even if it did come from an inside-out place of really feeling like we needed two films to tell the story, I think audiences find it cynical. Even if its intentions are earnest, which they were. They feel like it’s a play to make them see two films instead of one.” The producer added: “We really put the burden on ourselves [now], even when it’s a big book, to transform it into a theatrical experience, to not take advantage of your audience’s patience, to make it as tight as we can. articles.content: American filmmaker Ava DuVernay is the first recipient of the London Critics’ Circle’s inaugural Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award. DuVernay, who this year has taken her most recent documentary, 14th , on the festival circuit, will accept the newly created honor from Mulvey herself at the London Critics’ Circle Film Awards ceremony in the British capital on Feb. 7. The Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award is designed to recognize “the most influential women in film, who are working to break the glass ceiling, change the cultural conversation, and be an example of what is possible for future generations,” according to London Critics’ Circle. DuVernay’s 14th — set to release in U.K. cinemas Nov. 27 before dropping on Netflix Dec. 4 — is an exploration of American democracy through the lens of the foundational 14th Amendment, exposing an unfinished battle to define America, now taking on drastic new dimensions. articles.title: ‘Meet the Parents’: THR’s 2000 Review
articles.summary: The comedy is "a crisply paced romp featuring pitch-perfect performances by adversarial leads Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller."
articles.content: On Oct. 6, 2000, moviegoers met Greg Focker and Co. for the first time as Meet the Parents hit theaters. The Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller comedy scored $330 million and launched a franchise that now totals four movies . The Hollywood Reporter’s original review is below: Proving that there’s life after Austin Powers , director Jay Roach finds his comic mojo winningly intact with Meet the Parents . The three words that instill instant dread in any prospective suitor are taken to their logical, side-splitting extreme in a crisply paced romp featuring pitch-perfect performances by adversarial leads Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller. With its built-in ability to strike a multigenerational, universal chord, this Universal and DreamWorks joint effort should handily emerge as one of the season’s top comedies. Taking its inspiration from an unreleased 1997 indie effort of the same name by Greg Glienna (who receives a shared story credit here with Mary Ruth Clarke), the new version shares very few details with the original aside from title and basic premise. Stiller plays nice guy Greg Focker (like that surname isn’t going to be milked for all it’s worth), who’s about to pop the question to his schoolteacher girlfriend Pam (Teri Polo) just when she receives word that her younger sister is getting married. With those proposal plans temporarily on hold, they drive to New York for the wedding, not to mention Greg’s introduction to Pam’s imposing dad, Jack (De Niro), and her sweetly supportive mom, Dina (Blythe Danner). A retired horticulturist who thinks nobody’s good enough for his first-born daughter, Jack has enough on Greg to question his merit as boyfriend material with his being a male nurse bearing an odd last name who doesn’t share Jack’s love of cats. articles.title: TV Ratings: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Records Another Huge Finale
articles.summary: Early ratings are at a 12-year high among adults 18-49 and even with last year in total viewers.
articles.content: The season 35 finale of Dancing With the Stars capped off a season of big ratings with the show’s best numbers of the fall. Early Nielsen ratings have the finale — which aired live coast to coast, a first for DWTS — averaging 9.2 million viewers, on par with preliminary numbers for last season’s final episode . The season 34 finale ended up at 9.43 million viewers after the addition of Nielsen’s big data component; final same-day numbers for Tuesday’s show will be available after Thanksgiving. The DWTS finale also scored the show’s best rating among adults 18-49 in more than a decade: It’s currently at 2.38 (equivalent to about 3.24 million people in the demographic), subject to adjustments. That’s the highest rating for a Dancing With the Stars episode since the season 19 finale in 2014 — when current host Alfonso Ribeiro won the mirror ball trophy — and the highest mark for a regularly scheduled network entertainment show (i.e., not a special like the Oscars or Grammys) since an episode of The Masked Singer in April 2020. The finale also scored a 15-year high among adults under 35 with a 2.86 rating — an almost unheard-of number for anything outside of live sports in the current broadcast environment. Pending updates for the finale, season 35 of DWTS averaged 7.19 million viewers, up about 11 percent from last year. The show’s 1.59 rating among adults 18-49 is up by almost 20 percent year to year. The latter number ranks first among all network shows this fall, excluding live sports, and leads second-place Survivor (0.86 rating) by a canyon-sized 86 percent margin. Should that hold, it would be the largest gap between a first- and second-place show in the 18-49 demo since the beginning of Nielsen’s electronic measurement in 1991. ABC says viewers cast a record-setting 86 million votes during the finale, up from 72 million for the season 34 closer. DWTS also generated the most social media engagements of any primetime program Tuesday.

articles.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed as Storm Descends on Northeast
articles.summary: The annual event is one of the most-watched TV events of the year for NBC.
articles.content: In an unprecedented move, the 100th edition of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City will be postponed until Saturday Nov. 28, Macy’s and NBC announced Wednesday. The decision comes as a powerful nor’easter storm is bearing down on the northeast, with potential wind gusts north of 60 miles per hour alongside heavy rain. It’s also a major headache for the broadcast partner NBC, with last year’s parade drawing over 34 million viewers between NBC and Peacock . Related Stories TV Amanda Seyfried, Robert De Niro and Timothee Chalamet to Host 'SNL' in December TV NBC to Air Princess of Wales Cancer Charity Documentary The parade is now expected to kick off on the Upper West Side at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday, with the floats, balloons and performers making their way down to Macy’s flagship store on 34th Street. NBC confirmed that it will broadcast the parade Saturday at 8:30 a.m. to all time zones; it will also stream on Peacock. “Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28,” an NBC spokesperson told The Hollywood Reporter . “More details to follow. In addition, NBC will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.” It’s also a logistical nightmare, with many performance groups and musical artists coming into town for the parade, and which may need to find alternative travel plans. The parade has never been canceled in its 100 years, though some of the iconic giant balloons have been grounded when there have been high winds. Balloons are supposed to be grounded if wind gusts top 34 miles per hour. In 1993, a Sonic the Hedgehog balloon was pushed into a lamppost amid high winds, injuring multiple people, and a similar incident occurred in 1997 with a Cat in the Hat balloon. articles.title: A+E Doubles Down on Microdramas With Snips Partnership (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The media brand is working with the company to adapt traditional entertainment projects into mobile-first vertical stories, with episodes no more than two minutes long.
articles.content: A+E is deepening its investment in the world of microdramas , most recently by inking a content partnership with the shortform video company Snips, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Under the auspices of the agreement, Snips will use its proprietary technology to adapt previously released television programs into mobile-first stories told in vertically oriented, short chapters, with cliffhangers galore, any extraneous material trimmed and episodes no more than two minutes long. The deal will allow the mobile app to stream roughly 50 true-crime and reality projects from A+E Global Media ’s library in this shortform format. “A+E Global Media has built some of the most obsessively watched unscripted and scripted storytelling in the industry for over four decades, and true crime and documentary content is some of the most naturally suited to how people actually watch on mobile — in short, sharp, story-driven bursts,” Snips co-founder and CEO Or Ben Shimon said in a statement . “We are delighted to bring some of A+E’s proven titles into our growing catalog.” The specific titles that will be adapted for the Snips audience were not immediately available. The Snips deal will provide A+E, which will retain ownership rights over projects, with data on viewership, completion rates, monetization and engagement for specific titles on the app. Meanwhile, the projects provided by A+E will augment the entertainment library available on Snips, which now includes around 1,700 titles. A+E Global Media is no stranger to the microdrama format, having first dipped its toes in the space in March when its label Lifetime released the project Tides of Temptation , executive produced by Taye Diggs. articles.title: Streaming Ratings: ‘Rings of Power,’ ‘Black Doves’ Open Lower After Long Gaps Between Seasons
articles.content: Two streaming shows starting new seasons after long breaks saw their U.S. viewing numbers fall off some compared to their most recent outings. The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power and Black Doves were two of the top three original series for the week of Jan. 9-15, but both drew smaller viewing time totals than their previous premiere weeks, both of which came in 2024. The Rings of Power had 866 million minutes of viewing for the the week on Prime Video, with 70 percent of that (about 606 million) devoted to the four episodes of season three that premiered Nov. 11. The 866 million minutes was off by 15 percent from 1.02 billion minutes for season two’s first week in August 2024. Internal viewing data reported by the two streamers also show declines for the two series: In renewing The Rings of Power for a fourth season, Prime Video said 33 million viewers worldwide had watched some of the new season over its first 12 days, compared to 40 million over 11 days for season two. Netflix reported 6.6 million global views for season two of Black Doves for the week; season one had 10.8 million for its first week. The No. 2 original series for the week was Marvel’s VisionQuest , which hit a high of 696 million viewing minutes on Disney+ for the week of its finale. articles.summary: The beloved motor show has been off air since co-host Andrew Flintoff was involved in a serious, on-set car crash in 2022.
articles.content: Top Gear is set to return to the BBC with entrepreneur, chef and self-proclaimed car fanatic Gordon Ramsay as its host. The U.K.’s beloved, long-running series has been off air since 2022 after co-host Andrew Flintoff was involved in an on-set car crash. He suffered serious facial and rib injuries when his open-top vehicle overturned on Top Gear ‘s test track. On Wednesday, the broadcaster confirmed that the world’s most celebrated motoring entertainment show (previously helmed by Jeremy Clarkson, James May and Richard Hammond) will be back on our screens in 2028. articles.title: TV Ratings: NBA Logs Winning Streak in First Month of the Season
articles.summary: Audiences on national media partners NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are up by 37 percent year to year.
articles.content: Like a jump shooter who can’t miss, the NBA is on a heater with TV audiences through the first month of its 2026-27 season. National telecasts of league games on NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are averaging 2.62 million viewers over the season’s first month, based on Nielsen ratings and Adobe Analytics figures for Peacock’s games. That’s a sizable, 37 percent increase over the same time frame last year — the first in the league’s current media rights deal with NBCUniversal, ESPN and Prime Video. Through last week, every national telecast had topped 1 million viewers, the first time that’s happened since 2023. Related Stories TV TV Ratings: CMA Awards Score Seven-Year High TV Streaming Ratings: Rough Week for Original Series, 'From' Remains No. 1 Overall That’s also the highest mark on record for the first month of an NBA season, excluding lockout-delayed starts in 1999 and 2011 (and with the caveat that changes in Nielsen measurement the past few years have tended to benefit live sports). NBC’s six national windows lead the way with an average of 4.5 million viewers (including streaming on Peacock), a 27 percent improvement over last season’s first month.. The network’s opening night game between the defending champion New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers (who acquired LeBron James during the offseason) averaged 7.71 million cross-platform viewers. The first eight games on Prime Video have averaged 2.05 million viewers, and ESPN is at 1.8 million viewers across 13 telecasts. Prime Video has grown by a huge 83 percent year to year, and ESPN’s games are up 13 percent. Prime Video has the youngest audience of the NBA’s three national media partners (the same is true for Prime relative to other NFL broadcasters); its median viewer age is a little under 46. ESPN and NBC (not including Peacock viewers) have a median age of about 53 for NBA games.

articles.title: Steven Hack, Original ‘Cats’ Castmember and Busy Onscreen Character Actor, Dies at 68
articles.summary: His credits ranged from ‘Jake and the Fatman’ and ‘Seinfeld’ to ‘Pam & Tommy’ and ‘Amsterdam.’
articles.content: Steven Hack, the theater veteran who spent five years on Broadway as an original castmember in Cats , then appeared as a character actor in dozens of films and TV shows, has died. He was 68. Hack died Thursday at home following what was described as “a sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” the Interact Theatre Company announced . He was a founding member of the North Hollywood-based group that launched in 1989. “Steven was a gifted and versatile performer, a superb graphic artist and a cherished member of our artistic family,” ITC directors Barry Heins and Walter Ware said in a statement. “His creativity and talent helped shape Interact in its earliest years, and his artistry, humor, warmth and generous spirit enriched everything he touched.” Related Stories Lifestyle "Sometimes You Just Have to Think: 'What Will Make People Laugh?'": Lolly Adefope on Gags, 'Ghosts' and Her West End Debut Business IATSE Reaches Tentative Agreement for Broadway Stagehands Born in St. Louis on April 20, 1958, Hack studied at CalArts and The American Academy of Dramatic Arts in Los Angeles. In 1978, he was a background dancer in the film version of Grease and appeared in the off-Broadway musical The Coolest Cat in Town . Hack was there when Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Cats opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on Oct. 7, 1982, and he portrayed several characters, including Coricopat, Mungojerrie, Carbucketty, Tumblebrutus and Pouncival, over the next five years. He toured with Michael Bennett’s A Chorus Line for nearly two years and then joined the Broadway production at the Shubert Theatre for one show only — its record-breaking 3,389th Great White Way performance on Sept. 29, 1983. (He did Cats that night, too.) Hack started showing up on television in the 1990s on shows including The Trials of Rosie O’Neill , Jake and the Fatman , Matlock , Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman , Married … With Children , Seinfeld , Mad About You and Caroline in the City . articles.title: ‘South Park’ Takes Aim at Jensen Huang, Nvidia Spy Scandal in Next Episode
articles.summary: The town hunts for a Chinese spy amid a series of mysterious power outages in Wednesday's episode.
articles.content: The espionage allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and America’s recent series of software outages and cyberattacks appear to be the next cultural targets to be mocked on South Park (rebranded South America for the current season). Wednesday’s episode is titled “City Endings.” The official description reads: “When mysterious power outages strike South America, the townspeople fear Chinese cyberattacks. It’s up to the boys to discover what’s really going on.” In a brief promo for the episode (watch it below), a local declares, “Someone in this town is a Chinese spy.” In another scene, Tuong Lu Kim, also known as the City Wok Guy, is announcing the grand opening of his new massage parlor called City Massage (a name which takes on a different meaning when you hear how co-creator Trey Parker voices it). Related Stories Business The Center of the News Universe Has Shifted to CNBC Business Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO The new episode will have its debut on Comedy Central at 10 p.m. ET and will stream on Thursday on Paramount+. South Park is coming off last year’s Emmy-winning season, which also set some modern-day ratings records for the show. The show has made appearances in the Nielsen streaming Top 10 this season but has come down a bit from last year’s highs, when the show pivoted into a series of topical attacks on the Trump administration. The series rebranded as South America to mock President Trump’s penchant for trying to rename geographic features.

articles.content: Kevin Kline will star opposite Meryl Streep in the limited series adaptation of Jonathan Franzen’s novel. In The Corrections , Kline will play Alfred Lambert, the patriarch of the family at the center of the story. The series will follow the three adult siblings who “desperately resist their mother’s wish for one last Christmas together — each undone by the delusional ambitions that were supposed to save them from becoming their parents.” Paramount TV Studios is producing The Corrections . Franzen is adapting his best-selling and National Book Award-winning 2001 novel. Cord Jefferson ( American Fiction, Watchmen ) will direct every episode. They executive produce with Mark Roybal and Paul Lee of Wiip, Nicole Clemens, Amy Sayres and Streep. Kline won the best supporting actor Oscar in 1989 for his role in A Fish Called Wanda . articles.title: Bob Iger Had Extramarital Affair and Got Employee Pregnant, Tell-All Says
articles.summary: The revelation comes from Robbie Whelan's upcoming unauthorized biography "The House of the Mouse" The post Bob Iger Had Extramarital Affair and Got Employee Pregnant, Tell-All Says appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The revelation comes from Robbie Whelan’s upcoming unauthorized biography “The House of the Mouse” Bob Iger had an extramarital affair and got an employee pregnant, an upcoming unauthorized biography charting the corporate history of Disney claims. The revelation is made in Robbie Whelan’s “The House of the Mouse,” which The New York Times got an advance copy of and reported on Wednesday. Whelan says the former Disney CEO had an affair with an ABC marketer in the 1990s when he was the head of ABC Entertainment, per the Times. Their relationship was consensual. (Iger divorced wife Susan Iger in 1994 and married his current wife Willow Bay in 1995.) The unnamed woman, Iger’s subordinate, became pregnant and “suffered through a traumatic termination procedure,” Whelan wrote. The author contrasted Iger’s personal behavior with his public support of the #MeToo movement in the 2010s, where powerful figures were held accountable for their inappropriate actions. The 75-year-old executive served as CEO of Disney twice, first succeeding Michael Eisner in 2005 until his contract expired in 2020. He returned for his second stint in November 2022 until he was succeeded by Josh D’Amaro last March. “Josh D’Amaro is an exceptional leader and the right person to become our next CEO,” Iger said of D’Amaro’s appointment at the time. “He has an instinctive appreciation of the Disney brand, and a deep understanding of what resonates with our audiences, paired with the rigor and attention to detail required to deliver some of our most ambitious projects. His ability to combine creativity with operational excellence is exemplary and I am thrilled for Josh and the company.” “The House of Mouse: Bob Iger and the War of Succession at Disney” will be released on Dec. 1.

articles.content: The three-hour finale scored the best ratings for any “Dancing With the Stars” episode in 12 years “Dancing With the Stars” leapt to its biggest audience all season with Tuesday’s Season 35 finale. The three-hour season closer, which saw Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach get crowned as the winning couple, scored 9.2 million viewers across platforms, according to live-plus-same-day Nielsen figures. The total viewership matches the Season 34 closer that scored 9.24 million viewers across ABC and Disney+, which marked the biggest audience “Dancing with the Stars” had seen since its Season 29 finale in 2020. However, the 2026 finale saw notable growth in the key broadcast demo among adults 18-49, with the closer scoring a 2.38 rating, rising 11% as compared to the 2.15 rating the Season 34 finale scored last year. The ratings marked the best result for any “DWTS” episode in 12 years, since host Alfonso Ribeiro and his partner Witney Carson took home the Mirrorball Trophy in 2014. That milestone boosted the finale to rank as the highest-rated entertainment telecast since the Oscars earlier this year. Overall, the ABC ballroom dancing competition show stands as the No. 1 entertainment series across TV for the third season in a row. The competition series has continued to soar among younger viewers, with the finale scoring a 2.86 rating among adults 18-34, marking its strongest performance in the demo in 15 years. In fact, ratings in the young adult demo for the Season 35 finale outpaced the combined ratings for this year’s VMAs and the Golden Globes. Additionally, fan voting hit a new high of over 86 million votes for the finale, rising 19% over last season’s record-breaking tally, marking the most votes ever for a single episode. The sheep might talk and solve crimes, but they look like real animals you’d find on any farm. articles.summary: With the 1983 classic newly available from Criterion, the director of photography looks back on working with director Philip Kaufman to create a great American epic.

Director Philip Kaufman’s adaptation of Tom Wolfe’s book, which traced the history of the test pilots who became the first astronauts, features immersive set pieces that are still as convincing as ever, in spite of decades of technological advancements since it was made. To revisit it via Criterion ‘s new 4K UHD physical media release is to experience one of the most groundbreaking and enduring films of all time. The new Criterion transfer was supervised by cinematographer Caleb Deschanel , who was still relatively early in his career when Kaufman tapped him to shoot “ The Right Stuff .” Deschanel didn’t have many feature credits, but the ones he did have were impressive: his early work included the stunning imagery of “The Black Stallion” and two Hal Ashby movies, “Being There” and the Rolling Stones concert film “Let’s Spend the Night Together.” He would earn the first of his six Academy Award nominations for “The Right Stuff.” Related Stories Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March Deschanel had met Kaufman years earlier when Deschanel was a film student at USC, and Kaufman was a young director working on the Western “The Great Northfield Minnesota Raid.” “A couple friends and I put on these rock shows at Shrine Auditorium, and he came to a couple of those,” Deschanel told IndieWire. Deschanel visited the set of “Minnesota” and stayed in touch with Kaufman, who called him around 10 years later with the offer to shoot “The Right Stuff.” “It was a dream come true,” Deschanel said, noting that he had always been an aviation buff who loved going to air shows with his father. articles.title: ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March
articles.summary: Neon is distributing Takashi Miike's take on police depravity, with Shun Oguri starring as a drug-addled detective.
articles.content: “Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo,” a Japan-set take on police decadence, will open in North America on March 5, 2027. Neon , the Oscar-winning studio behind “Anora” and “Parasite,” is distributing the film . Directed by Takashi Miike, the Japanese auteur behind “Audition” and “13 Assassins,” “” Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo ” stars Shun Oguri (“Godzilla v. Kong”), Lily James (“Pam and Tommy”), and WWE star Liv Morgan. It follows a veteran police detective Yabuki (Oguri), who is struggling with drug addiction, gambling debts, and guilt over past misdeeds, as he chases a shadowy killer tied to organized crime through Tokyo. His case ends up intersecting with that of an American FBI agent (James), who’s hunting a missing tourist (Morgan). Related Stories ‘The Trip’ Returns for Fifth Installment, Next Sending Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon to Frigid Arctic Circle ‘The Holy Boy’ Review: A Teenage Boy Heals People with His Touch in an Eerie Italian Horror Movie About the Price of Avoiding Your Pain The film had its world premiere at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival, where it earned mixed notices, with some reviewers faulting it as overstuffed. Neon is in the midst of a busy fall, with the indie studio releasing awards contenders such as “All of a Sudden,” “Fjord,” “Paper Tiger,” and “Artificial,” so it makes sense that it would opt to have “Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo” come out in the spring. “Bad Lieutenant” first entered the cinematic vernacular with Abel Ferrara’s 1992 crime thriller that was so boundary-pushing (a nun is raped) it received an NC-17 rating. It also offered up Harvey Keitel at his most unhinged and committed, playing a cop who broke really, really bad. articles.title: ‘The Trip’ Returns for Fifth Installment, Next Sending Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon to Frigid Arctic Circle
articles.summary: Michael Winterbottom's "The Trip to the Northern Lights" has been acquired by the Independent Film Company and will be released in theaters April 9, 2027.
articles.content: What does “Michael Caine” sound like in the freezing cold? We’re about to find out with the just-announced release of “ The Trip to the Northern Lights,” which is the reunion of Steve Coogan , Rob Brydon , and director Michael Winterbottom for what is the fifth installment of “The Trip” franchise of miniseries/movies. Independent Film Company and Sapan Studio picked up the U.S. rights to the fifth “Trip” film (IFC has released all four of the other films into theaters in the U.S.) and will release it theatrically on April 9, 2027. It will have been nearly seven years since the release of the last feature, and it sees Brydon now at 60 and Coogan at 59, so we’re guessing their ages may have made their wit and appetites even more ornery since.
